contract.known_boundary: Detect acceleration backends actually available on the current device, select only a compatible backend, expose an explicit CPU fallback and preserve backend/model incompatibility instead of inferring acceleration from the operating system alone.
contract.non_equivalence_policy: Operating-system support, a backend compiled into a runtime, device availability, model compatibility and measured acceleration are distinct facts and must not be treated as semantically interchangeable.
contract.runtime_selection_policy: Selection must be probe-driven and fail closed: a backend is eligible only after runtime availability and model compatibility are confirmed; otherwise the adapter must report unsupported/unavailable and use an explicit compatible fallback.

candidates.backend_family: GGUF/ggml with CPU plus Metal, CUDA, HIP, Vulkan, SYCL, OpenCL, Hexagon and other native backends
candidates.known_constraint: Full-repository preflight is BLOCKED. The backend-only scan is complete but remains REVIEW because regeneration tooling can execute subprocesses and the scoped tree has no supported dependency manifest.

candidates.backend_family: ONNX execution providers including CPU, CUDA, TensorRT, OpenVINO, QNN, NNAPI, CoreML, DirectML, WebNN, WebGPU and XNNPACK
candidates.known_constraint: The provider-only scan remains REVIEW and incomplete because the scanner reached its 800-file budget; supply-chain/vulnerability admission therefore remains open.

candidates.backend_family: llama.cpp browser integration using WebAssembly SIMD and WebGPU
candidates.known_constraint: The source contains an unscanned llama.cpp submodule, precompiled WASM and process-execution tooling. WebGPU and multithreading also depend on browser/device capabilities and deployment headers.

research_findings.llama_cpp: Pinned llama.cpp documents broad ggml backend coverage. Its Android binding detects host CPU features and supports Arm SME2/x86 AMX, while the pinned tree also documents Apple XCFramework packaging.
research_findings.onnxruntime: Pinned ONNX Runtime is a cross-platform accelerator. The provider registry contains CPU, CUDA, TensorRT, OpenVINO, QNN, NNAPI, CoreML, DirectML, WebNN, WebGPU and XNNPACK among other providers.
research_findings.web: ONNX Runtime Web exposes WebAssembly/WebGPU integration. wllama provides an independent browser candidate relative to ONNX Runtime, using WebAssembly SIMD and optional WebGPU offload over the llama.cpp ecosystem.
research_findings.raspberry_pi: llama.cpp provides Linux/ARM-native research coverage and ONNX Runtime v1.30.0 publishes a Linux AArch64 artifact. These are architecture-level signals only; no Raspberry Pi board/OS/model performance certification is asserted.
research_findings.security: No candidate is security admitted. Full llama.cpp is BLOCKED; full ONNX Runtime and wllama are REVIEW. Backend-scoped llama.cpp and ONNX Runtime are also REVIEW, with ONNX incomplete because the scanner hit its file budget.

decision.next_action: Keep discovery depth closed but admission open. Define the runtime capability-probe and fallback contract, isolate smaller provider/backend scopes where possible, complete security/SBOM/OSV gates, then run target-specific hardware and model-compatibility validation.
